record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let X be an affine scheme over k, let g be a semisimple finite-dimensional Lie algebra over k, let Γ act on X and g by automorphisms, and set M = M(X,g)^Γ. Describe the first cohomology group H1(M,V) for a general M-module V, extending the partial results known for some equivariant map algebras and locally finite modules. In particular, describe H1(M,Mad) for the adjoint M-module, equivalently the derivations of M modulo inner derivations.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

4.3.2. Cohomology. Assume g is semisimple. The formulas for ExtM (V1 , V2 ) proven in [NS] have a cohomological interpretation since ExtM (V1 , V2 ) ≃ H1(M, Homk(V1 , V2)). One can therefore expect that it should be possible to describe the first cohomol- ogy group H1 (M, V ) for a general M-module V . For some equivariant map alge- bras M, including multiloop algebras, and locally-finite M-modules, this is done in [NP]. A particular instance of this question is the adjoint module Mad , for which H1 (M, Mad ) = Derk (M)/ IDer(M).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let $X$ be an affine scheme over $k$ with coordinate ring $A = \mathcal{O}(X)$, and let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over $k$. Let $\Gamma$ be a group acting by automorphisms on $X$ (equivalently, on $A$) and by Lie algebra automorphisms on $\mathfrak{g}$. The equivariant map algebra associated with this data is
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{g})^\Gamma = (\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma,$$
the fixed-point subalgebra under the induced diagonal $\Gamma$-action, with its natural Lie algebra structure inherited from $\mathfrak{g}\otimes A$.

For an arbitrary $M$-module $V$ (not assumed locally finite, finite-dimensional, or of any other restricted type), give an explicit description of the first Lie algebra cohomology group $H^1(M,V)$ in terms of the data $(X,\mathfrak{g},\Gamma,V)$.

In particular, taking $V = M^{\mathrm{ad}}$ to be the adjoint module, describe
$$H^1(M, M^{\mathrm{ad}}) \;\cong\; \mathrm{Der}_k(M)/\mathrm{IDer}(M),$$
i.e., compute the space of outer derivations of $M$ in terms of $(X,\mathfrak{g},\Gamma)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the survey on equivariant map algebras. Partial results are known: H^1 has been computed for some equivariant map algebras (including multiloop algebras) and for locally finite modules by Neher–Savage and collaborators, and the derivation algebra has been studied in the untwisted case M = g⊗A and via étale descent of derivations (Neher–Pianzola). A complete description for general M-modules V and a full computation of Der_k(M)/IDer(M) in the equivariant setting does not appear to have been achieved.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: For some equivariant map algebras M, including multiloop algebras, and locally-finite M-modules, this is done in [NP]. A particular instance of this question is the adjoint module M^ad, for which H^1(M,M^ad) = Der_k(M)/IDer(M).
status_evidence.claim: H^1(M,V) is known only for restricted classes; the general case is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Étale descent of derivations
status_evidence.snippet: Étale descent of derivations is used to compute derivation algebras in equivariant settings.
status_evidence.claim: Derivations of equivariant map algebras have only been partially computed.
